scope: independent read-only static review, no new GPU execution

findings.finding: Texture2D shader bindings accept sampled Texture3D/array/multisample or non-color view descriptions; current unsafe contract does not exclude these.
findings.suggestion: Validate image_type TYPE_2D, array_layers1, samples TYPE_1, COLOR aspect for blue_noise and images; permit legal multiple mip levels.

findings.finding: Runtime/partially-bound/variable-count/update-after-bind flags do not imply enabled sampled-image non-uniform indexing. Headless init requests it, arbitrary VulkanDevice creation may omit it.
findings.suggestion: Record actual enabled shader_sampled_image_array_non_uniform_indexing in DeviceCapabilities and require it when actual SPIR-V declares this capability; retain headless result scope.

findings.finding: Draining and abandoning uploads, recreating GpuTextRenderer while CPU glyph cache is warm, or switching GPU renderer with same CPU state can produce a fresh cleared atlas and glyph batches with no uploads. Current API cannot recover cached RGBA.
findings.suggestion: Specify upload ownership/ack/retry; add recovery/invalidate/reupload mechanism or explicit rejection requiring atlas initialization. Test failure and recreate paths; this is distinct from stale-generation rejection.

findings.finding: Fence wait does not advance global completed_epoch, readback sync path therefore adds vkDeviceWaitIdle after fence each frame. submits1 true; only wait-once wording false.
findings.suggestion: Provide narrowly unsafe read-after-specific-completion path with host invalidation, or disclose/count extra device idle. Never mark all global submits complete from one fence.

findings.finding: colored>100 and cold==warm do not prove atlas alpha/glyph sentinel, each loaded fallback font, combining/RTL layout, or 2x geometry. Candidate HLSL has opposite sentinels from new CPU assumptions; only original SPIR-V can arbitrate.
findings.suggestion: Add synthetic atlas alpha probe contrasting stream0/MAX, real glyph partial transparency/hole checks, per-script face/layout checks and scale bounds/generation assertions; preserve original binary evidence.
